expected_metric: Attributable warm replies and eventual purchases after domain health confirmed or corrected
hypothesis: 80 cold sends with zero replies from a new or insufficiently warmed domain is more likely a deliverability failure than a messaging failure — SPF/DKIM/DMARC auth and domain warm-up are the highest-leverage diagnostic checks before rewriting copy.
observed_problem: Cold email campaigns with well-written copy still land in spam when domain reputation is damaged by missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC, purchased lists, or sudden volume spikes from new domains without warm-up.
smallest_safe_change: Run a SPF/DKIM/DMARC validation check on nebulacomponents.com and the AgentMail sending domain; check Google Postmaster or MXToolbox for domain reputation score before changing any copy.
stop_condition: Stop volume if domain reputation score degrades further or bounce rate exceeds 5%
validation_window: 7 days from first send after confirmed domain health
why_nebula: Nebula has sent 80 trigger-based emails with 0 warm replies — the most common cause of that exact symptom is domain deliverability failure, not copy. This evidence maps directly to the audit_to_payment_conversion bottleneck upstream: if emails never reach inboxes, no audit requests, no payments.
